column1: # SP-6b (section 7): AN INDEPENDENT PRESIDENTIAL CANDIDATE'S BALLOT ACCESS, 2024 - READ from NASS's "Summary: State Laws Regarding Presidential Ballot
# Access for the General Election" (updated July 2024; raw/ballot_access/nass_summary_ballot_access_laws_president_072924.pdf), one row a jurisdiction.
# Tools/us_ballot_prep.pl holds every row to the summary's own text: each quote must occur in that state's section (whitespace ignored, the
# extraction splitting figures such as "5 ,000"), and every figure a rule names must stand in its quote. Nothing here is a figure of its own: a count is
# the summary's, a formula's base is read from the catalog on disk or BILLED, a deadline is the summary's rule applied to 5 Nov 2024.
# signatures:  count N                      the summary's number (a range's floor where it gives one: ME 4,000-6,000, WI 2,000-4,000)
#              pct P BASE                   P % of BASE, rounded up
#              lesser P BASE N [bound B]    the lesser of P % of BASE and N; where BASE is not on disk, B (on disk, never above BASE) decides it
#                                           when P % of B already reaches N - else BILLED
#              billed WHY                   no count can be read
# deadline:    days N                       N days before polling day
#              date MM-DD                   the date the summary names
#              nth K DAY MON                the K-th DAY of MON (K = last for the last)
#              after K DAY MON DAY2 J       the J-th DAY2 after the K-th DAY of MON
#              mondays N                    the N-th Monday before polling day
#              business N MM-DD             the N-th business day after MM-DD
# fee:         usd N add | usd N alt        a fee beside the petition (add) or instead of it (alt); none: the summary names none; billed WHY
# BASE: pres2020 (president_by_state.csv, 2020 votes_total), house2022 (house_by_state.csv, 2022 votes_total), or a base not on disk, named.
